findings.root_cause: The method constraint was retained only in the first OR branch while the new retry-count branch is globally scoped.
findings.suggested_fix: Place `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` outside the `OR`, so both the expired-date and exhausted-retry predicates are restricted to SMS reminders.
findings.title: Retry cleanup deletes reminders for non-SMS methods
findings.trigger: The SMS cron runs while any EMAIL or WHATSAPP WorkflowReminder has retryCount greater than 1, such as after another worker or data operation uses the generic retryCount field on the shared model.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines R38-R42 add a second OR branch with only `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` and no `method` constraint. findings.body: The catch block throws a new unhandled error, the endpoint returns an error, and all later reminders in the loop are left unprocessed until a subsequent cron run.
findings.failure_mode: Error handling itself rejects the handler instead of isolating the failed reminder and continuing the loop.
findings.impact: The catch block throws a new unhandled error, the endpoint returns an error, and all later reminders in the loop are left unprocessed until a subsequent cron run.
findings.root_cause: A potentially throwing database operation is awaited inside the scheduling catch block without any secondary error handling.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard retry bookkeeping with its own try/catch and use a conditional `updateMany` when a concurrently deleted row should be treated as a no-op, while logging both the scheduling and bookkeeping failures.
findings.title: Failure bookkeeping can abort the entire cron handler
findings.trigger: The retry update fails, for example because booking cancellation deleted the reminder after findMany or because the database write is temporarily unavailable.
findings.verifier_reason: Lines R190-R197 show an unguarded `await prisma.workflowReminder.update()` inside the catch block. If this update throws (e.g., reminder was deleted by concurrent booking cancellation), the exception propagates, aborting the handler and leaving remaining reminders unprocessed. The trigger is realistic since booking cancellations delete workflow reminders.

pr.body:
## What does this PR do?

Right now when SMS fails to send because of whatever reason (e.g. invalid phone number), we are trying to keep scheduling it in our corn job until the date is reached. This PR introduces a retry count, after scheduling failed twice we delete the workflow reminder.
pr.title: fix: add retryCount to workflowReminder

raw_findings.body: The SMS cron permanently deletes the unrelated email or WhatsApp reminder, so it cannot be scheduled or canceled through its normal worker.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A retry count alone satisfies deleteMany regardless of the reminder's delivery method.
raw_findings.impact: The SMS cron permanently deletes the unrelated email or WhatsApp reminder, so it cannot be scheduled or canceled through its normal worker.
raw_findings.root_cause: The method constraint was retained only in the first OR branch while the new retry-count branch is globally scoped.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Place `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` outside the `OR`, so both the expired-date and exhausted-retry predicates are restricted to SMS reminders.
raw_findings.title: Retry cleanup deletes reminders for non-SMS methods
raw_findings.trigger: The SMS cron runs while any EMAIL or WHATSAPP WorkflowReminder has retryCount greater than 1, such as after another worker or data operation uses the generic retryCount field on the shared model.

raw_findings.body: Both writes store the same next value, so multiple failed attempts count as one and the reminder receives more provider attempts than the configured two-failure limit.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Last-write-wins updates undercount concurrent scheduling failures.
raw_findings.impact: Both writes store the same next value, so multiple failed attempts count as one and the reminder receives more provider attempts than the configured two-failure limit.
raw_findings.root_cause: The counter is calculated from the stale value selected before scheduling rather than incremented atomically in the database.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use Prisma's atomic increment operation, `retryCount: { increment: 1 }`, at both newly added retry-update sites.
raw_findings.title: Retry increments lose failures when cron executions overlap
raw_findings.trigger: Two authenticated cron requests overlap, read the same reminder retryCount, and both fail to schedule it before either update completes.

raw_findings.body: The catch block throws a new unhandled error, the endpoint returns an error, and all later reminders in the loop are left unprocessed until a subsequent cron run.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Error handling itself rejects the handler instead of isolating the failed reminder and continuing the loop.
raw_findings.impact: The catch block throws a new unhandled error, the endpoint returns an error, and all later reminders in the loop are left unprocessed until a subsequent cron run.
raw_findings.root_cause: A potentially throwing database operation is awaited inside the scheduling catch block without any secondary error handling.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Guard retry bookkeeping with its own try/catch and use a conditional `updateMany` when a concurrently deleted row should be treated as a no-op, while logging both the scheduling and bookkeeping failures.
raw_findings.title: Failure bookkeeping can abort the entire cron handler
raw_findings.trigger: The retry update fails, for example because booking cancellation deleted the reminder after findMany or because the database write is temporarily unavailable.

raw_findings.body: The row records a scheduling failure even though an external SMS is queued; after the retry threshold it can be deleted locally while the Twilio message remains active and untracked.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Post-provider persistence errors are misclassified as failed SMS scheduling attempts.
raw_findings.impact: The row records a scheduling failure even though an external SMS is queued; after the retry threshold it can be deleted locally while the Twilio message remains active and untracked.
raw_findings.root_cause: The catch block covers both the provider call and the post-success database update, so it cannot distinguish a scheduling failure from a persistence failure.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Limit retry-count updates to failures or empty results from `twilio.scheduleSMS`; handle persistence failures after a successful provider response separately and preserve or reconcile the returned SID.
raw_findings.title: A successful Twilio schedule can consume the retry budget
raw_findings.trigger: Twilio successfully creates the scheduled SMS, but the following database update that sets `scheduled` and `referenceId` throws and a subsequent retry-count update succeeds.

raw_findings.body: The next cron invocation deletes the row before its send date even though Twilio has accepted the SMS, losing the reference needed to cancel that SMS if the booking is canceled or rescheduled.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A mixed success/failure state produced by overlapping workers is treated as an exhausted unscheduled reminder and removed prematurely.
raw_findings.impact: The next cron invocation deletes the row before its send date even though Twilio has accepted the SMS, losing the reference needed to cancel that SMS if the booking is canceled or rescheduled.
raw_findings.root_cause: The retry-count deletion predicate does not verify that the reminder is still unscheduled.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Restrict the exhausted-retry deletion branch to `scheduled: false`; also make failure updates conditional on the reminder still being unscheduled.
raw_findings.title: Retry cleanup can delete a successfully scheduled SMS record
raw_findings.trigger: Overlapping cron requests process a reminder at retryCount 1, one provider call succeeds while another fails, and their field-specific updates leave the row with `scheduled: true` and `retryCount: 2`.

finding.trigger: Two authenticated cron requests overlap, read the same reminder retryCount, and both fail to schedule it before either update completes.
finding.verifier_reason: The claim requires two overlapping cron executions to read the same stale retryCount. The cron runs every 15 minutes per the GitHub workflow. While theoretically possible, the scenario requires precise timing overlap and both failing. The practical likelihood is low, and the impact (extra retry attempts) is minor. The claim is speculative without evidence of actual concurrent execution patterns.

finding.trigger: Overlapping cron requests process a reminder at retryCount 1, one provider call succeeds while another fails, and their field-specific updates leave the row with `scheduled: true` and `retryCount: 2`.
finding.verifier_reason: This describes the same root cause as candidate 0: the retry-count deletion predicate at R38-R42 lacks a `method: SMS` constraint and lacks a `scheduled: false` check. Both candidates identify that the second OR branch can delete records it shouldn't. The fix would be the same: add method and scheduled constraints to the retry branch.
